name: LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS ClaritySurge Surgical Ocular
description:
The ClaritySurge is a medical-grade precision ocular implant engineered specifically for surgical and diagnostic professionals, replacing the natural eye with a multi-focal synthetic lens capable of continuous zoom from macro to 200x optical magnification. A tissue-analysis overlay reads spectral reflectance data in real time, flagging necrotic tissue, vascular anomalies, and foreign material through a color-coded HUD layer transparent enough to not obstruct fine motor work. Vein-mapping mode projects a live subsurface vasculature render up to 12mm deep, eliminating the need for external imaging during delicate procedures.

ClaritySurge units are standard equipment for Tier 3–5 surgical staff at Meridian's licensed medical institutions, and Lazarus offers subsidized installation packages through hospital procurement contracts. Among surgeons they carry a quiet professional prestige—a pair of ClaritySurge eyes signals serious clinical commitment, not aesthetic vanity—and the waiting list for full biocompatibility-optimized units at premium clinics runs six months.
installation_requirements: Board-certified ocular surgeon, full OR suite, Lazarus-certified installation technician required for warranty validation
rejection_risk: Minimal — Lazarus biocompatible polymer housing with pharmaceutical-grade anti-rejection surface treatment; lowest rejection rate in class
maintenance: Annual Lazarus clinic calibration mandatory for medical licensing compliance; lens array self-cleaning via integrated microfluidic flush

side_effects: Persistent involuntary tissue-analysis overlay activation in non-clinical settings, making casual social interaction visually cluttered
Zoom-lock incidents where magnification fails to return to baseline without manual reset
Mild depth perception recalibration period of 2–4 weeks post-installation
Documented cases of vein-mapping mode activating during intimate contact, which users consistently describe as psychologically distressing
cultural_context: In Meridian's medical community, ClaritySurge eyes are a professional marker as legible as a white coat—surgeons wearing them are taken seriously, and those without them in high-tier institutions are quietly considered behind the curve. A secondary market exists among non-medical users who value the recording and zoom capabilities, though Lazarus' licensing verification makes gray-market units difficult to maintain.

story_hooks: A surgeon's ClaritySurge recorded something during an operation they weren't supposed to witness—now the recording is missing and so is the surgeon

Black-market ClaritySurge units are appearing in the Shelf without Lazarus licensing, meaning someone is manufacturing unlicensed copies with degraded tissue-analysis calibration—dangerous in the wrong hands
